Entity: Backup ZIP (content archive of all referenced attachments)

FR-002: No aggregate ZIP content on EC2 disk; S3 as materialization area
FR-003: Presigned download URL TTL 15min, regenerable per request
FR-007: Cross-backend restore (S3 ZIP restores to local backend and vice versa)
FR-015: Serialized operations — single in-flight job per active backend
FR-019: SHA256 as logical key in manifest; stored_filenames array for dedup
FR-020: Backup must backfill content_sha256 for null-hash attachments
Data Model: Phase 1 structs, interfaces, flows for S3 backup
Go struct: backup.Manifest (version, created_at, source_environment, entries[])
Go struct: server.Job (ID, Kind, State, Processed, Total, DownloadURL, SkippedEntries)
Go struct: BackupJobManager (mutex, activeByBackend map, LRU history cap=50)
Go interface: storage.S3Capable (GetRange, PresignGet, UploadFromReader, ListWithMetadata, DeleteMany)
DB index: idx_attachments_content_sha256 on attachments(content_sha256)
Data flow: streaming backup S3 (io.Pipe, zip.Writer, multipart upload, presign)
Data flow: restore cross-backend (upload ZIP, Range GETs, fan-out Put per stored_filename)
Research: Phase 0 technical decisions R1-R9 for S3 streaming backup
R1: io.Pipe + manager.Uploader for streaming ZIP to S3 without disk
R2: s3.NewPresignClient + PresignGetObject TTL 15min; no proxy via backend
R3: ZIP restore needs io.ReaderAt; S3 path uses Range GETs; local uses temp file
R4: manifest.json written as last ZIP entry; JSON format; stored_filenames array
R5: compute SHA256 via io.TeeReader during backup; persist via BackfillSHA256()
R6: in-memory BackupJobManager, no SQLite persistence, LRU bounded history
R7: startup sweep of _backup-tmp/ objects older than 24h via ListObjectsV2 + DeleteObjects
